sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
The player is a 3x3 blue ring, with a charcoal-colored "eye" at (16,17) — the right-center of the sprite, i.e., facing RIGHT. The eye hasn't moved even once, and the player hasn't moved either.
New hypothesis: the arrow keys rotate the facing direction, and the player automatically moves 1 step in the facing direction on each action tick (or on each step). The player is facing RIGHT, and there's a wall to the right → blocked → stays still. But the eye should rotate when the keys are pressed… yet the eye hasn't moved.
Or: the arrow keys move the player in the pressed direction, but only if the player is "awake." The player is asleep until…?
Or: the arrow keys move the player 1 cell (3px) in the pressed direction, but the game is checking the destination cell using the eye's position. The eye is at (16,17). Pressing DOWN: destination (17,17)='b' (the player's own pixel) → blocked by itself? Pressing LEFT: (16,16)='b' → blocked. Pressing UP: (15,17)='b' → blocked. Pressing RIGHT: (16,18)='g' → wall → blocked. Everything is blocked by the player's own body or by walls!
This would explain it if the game is treating the player as a 1x1 at the eye's position, and the blue ring is just decoration… but in that case, the player would never be able to move (its own ring blocks 3 directions, and a wall blocks the 4th).
Hmm, unless the game is moving the player as a 3x3 block and checking the leading edge. DOWN: leading edge row 18, columns 15-17 = B,B,B → open. Should move. But it didn't.
I'm really stuck on the theory. Let me try a different kind of probe: press RIGHT (toward the wall) and see if the bar's behavior changes (e.g., blocked moves consume more bar, or the eye moves). Actually, let me try a sequence that might trigger movement under the "facing" hypothesis: if the keys rotate the facing and the player moves in the facing direction on the next tick, then after pressing LEFT (facing left?), the player should move left on the next action. The eye is still facing right, so that's not it.
Wait wait wait. Let me reconsider. What if the arrow keys are moving the player, but the player is a 3x3, and the game is checking the destination 3x3 block, and the wall set is {W, w, g, G, B} — i.e., everything except the player's own colors is a wall?? In that case, the destination block must be empty (no pixels at all)? The black background is a single connected node (node 0, 3429 px) — the "background." If the game is treating the background as a wall, then every cell is a wall (the maze is drawn on top of the background), and the player can never move. That can't be right either.
Let me try yet another angle: maybe this game is a "Minesweeper/number"-style logic puzzle, and the arrow keys are selecting a cell (a hidden cursor), and the M bar is a timer. The cursor isn't visible… but maybe the cursor is the 'c' pixel! The 'c' at (16,17) might not be the player's eye but a cursor/selector! And the blue 3x3 is a "start" marker!
If 'c' is a cursor that moves 1 pixel (or 1 cell) with the arrow keys… but 'c' is at (16,17) in every frame. It hasn't moved.
Hmm, unless the cursor only moves when…?
Okay, let me try a completely different approach: brute-force a longer sequence and watch for any change. For example, try [RIGHT, RIGHT, RIGHT] (into the wall) and see if the player bounces or the eye moves. If nothing happens, try [UP, LEFT, DOWN, RIGHT] (a loop) and see if the eye rotates.
Actually — wait. Let me reconsider the possibility that the player is moving 1 pixel per action, and the game is checking the destination pixel against the wall set {W,w,g,G,c}, and 'c' is included in the wall set. The player's eye 'c' is at (16,17). If the game is moving the player's "position" = the eye's position, 1 pixel per action:
- DOWN: (17,17) = 'b' → not in the wall set → should move.
Nope.
What if the wall set = {W,w,g,G,b,c} (everything non-black is a wall)? In that case, the player (positioned at the eye (16,17)):
- DOWN: (17,17)='b' → wall → blocked.
- UP: (15,17)='b' → blocked.
- LEFT: (16,16)='b' → blocked.
- RIGHT: (16,18)='g' → blocked.
Everything is blocked! And the player can never move. But then the game would be impossible… unless the player's position isn't the eye.
What if the player's position is the top-left (15,15), and it moves 3 pixels, and the game is checking the destination 3x3 block against the wall set {W,w,g,G,b,c}?
- DOWN: block rows 18-20, columns 15-17 = all 'B' → not a wall → should move.
It didn't move.
I give up on the theory. Let me gather more data: try RIGHT (into the wall). If the bar's consumption is different, or if something changes, that's a signal.
